California Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law Assembly Bill 435 titled “Vehicles: child passenger restraints”

California will require all children ages 8 to 16 to ride in a car booster seat unless they pass a 5 step fit test. This takes effect January 1, 2027

Noncompliant drivers can face fines of nearly $500 for each child who is not properly secured

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, a child in that age range must be secured in an appropriate child passenger restraint system, car seat or booster. A seat belt only counts as “proper” if the child passes all five steps of the new 5-step fit test in that specific vehicle and seating position

The 5 steps:

1. Sitting all the way back against the vehicle seat
2. Knees bend over the edge of the seat
3. Shoulder belt snugly crosses the center of the chest and shoulder (not the neck)
4. Lap belt is as low as possible and touches the thighs
5. The child can stay seated that way for the whole trip

If they fail any step, they need a booster seat even if they are 16 years old or residents will face fines
